thread:
leo: FYI — after the 3f9d7c merge today's canary and CI perf runs show ~2x p95 latency on SSE streaming for tool-calling flows. Repro in canary and ci/perf. :eyes:

leo: Quick profile (canary, 512 tokens, toolcall enabled):
```
samples  |  function
---------------------
32%      | serialize_toolcall
28%      | sse_flush_builder
20%      | runtime_dispatch_loop
10%      | kernel_select_router
5%       | kv_prefetch
5%       | other
```

deploy-bot: deploy 3f9d7c -> canary succeeded (2026-03-18 08:12 UTC)

nora: Is the serialization path from PR #842 the only change in that deploy?

sam: No, we merged two stack changes: #842 (toolcall framing + fast-serialize) and #839 (kernel-router heuristics). Both landed in the same window. CI perf only pointed at higher SSE tail, not CPU count change.

zhou: I ran `bench/sse_stream` locally with a tracer. Fast-serialize reduces allocations but appears to increase single-request wall time when tool payloads are present — likely extra copy + sync before flush. Local flamegraph: https://flame.local/xyz (artifact attached).

infra-ci: ci/perf: run 1245, 1246, 1247 all failed threshold. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/1247/artifacts/perf-report.html

leo: This is a rollout blocker for the hosted API. Plan: pause rollout, bisect which of the two PRs is responsible, try a canary revert for the serialization change first.

nora: also check the kv-prefetch TTL tweak from #835 earlier — could be interacting (prefetch thrash = extra kernel churn).

sam: Quick micro-experiment idea: flip `coalesceWrites` -> false in sse writer to force immediate flush of toolcall frames and re-run perf. If p95 improves, the problem is flush timing.

sanjeev: ack, I'll monitor production traces and TCP metrics. Noting that one infra change toggled `tcp_nodelay` accidentally last week — double-checking egress buffering.

leo: I started a bisect branch: `bisect/3f9d7c-serialize-vs-kernel`. Assigning sam -> serialize, zhou -> kernel-router.

sam: running targeted bench (no-parallelization) with and without fast-serialize:
```
perf record -F 99 -g -- ./bin/bench_sse --toolcall=true --tokens=512
# then flamegraph
```
I'll post flamegraphs in ~45m.

qa-bot: Marked thread as rollout-blocker and set priority=P0.

leo: If we confirm serialize path is culprit, prefer a minimal revert of the copy/sync in `serialize_toolcall` (avoid full revert of framing logic). Would like a canary revert by EOD.

zhou: Kernel-router also changed candidate scoring (`score += recent_prefetch_weight`) — if that pushes a less-optimized kernel for common sequence lengths, throughput per-request can regress even with same CPU. I'll add a test to force kernel autoselect off.

sam: temp patch I tried locally (disable fast-serialize) reduced p95 by ~45% on my machine. Will push results.

leo: tagging @sanjeev and eng-oncall to watch canary. Leaving notes in the rollback playbook if we need emergency revert.

sanjeev: watching logs, setting alert for SSE p95 > 300ms.

leo: action items: 1) pause rollout (done), 2) sam/zhou bisect + perf artifacts, 3) sanjeev monitor prod, 4) open minimal revert PR if serialize patch is the root.

nora: thanks — ping me when bisect narrows.

sam: pushing perf artifacts now, will update thread with flamegraph and a minimal PR suggestion. :thumbsup:

leo: good. keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the rollback/bisect.
